questions.q: The coefficient of $x^{256}$ in the expansion of \left(1 - x\right)101\left(x^{2} + x + 1\right)100$ is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

\left(1 - x\right)101 \left($x^{2} + x + 1\right)100$

$= \left($1 - x\right)100\left($x^{2} + x + 1\right)100\left($1 - x\right)$

$= \left[ \left(1 - x\right) \left($x^{2} + x + 1\right)\right]100 $\cdot \left($1 - x\right)$

$= \left($1 - x^{3}\right)100 $\cdot\left($1 - x\right)$

$= \mathop{\left($1 - x^{3}\right)100 ⏟}_{Notermofx^{256}} - \mathop{x\left($1 - x^{3}\right)100 ⏟}_{wefindcofficientofx^{255}}$

Now,

\left(1 - x^{3}\right)100 = C0 100 - C1 100 x^{3} + C2 100 x^{6} - . . . - C85 100 \left(-x^{255}\right)$

$⇒ x\left(1 - x^{3}\right)100 = C0 100 x - C1 100 x^{4} + C2 100 x^{7} - . . . + C85 100 x^{256}$

Required coefficient

$= C85 100 = C15 100$

for $r = 8$ term is free from $'x'$
${T}_{9} = C8 16 \dfrac{1}{\sin^{8} \theta\cos^{8} \theta}$
${T}_{9} = C8 16 \dfrac{28}{\left(\sin 2\theta\right)8}$
In $\theta \in \left[\dfrac{π}{8}, \dfrac{π}{4}\right], {l}_{1} = C8 16 {2}^{8}$~($∵$~Minimum value of~${l}_{1}$~at~$\theta = \dfrac{π}{4}$)

$\dfrac{l2}{l1} = \dfrac{C8 16 . {2}^{8}{2}^{4}}{C8 16 . {2}^{8}} = 16$

\left(5 + x\right)500 + x\left(5 + x\right)499 + x^{2}\left(5 + x\right)498 + \ldots \ldots + x^{500}, x > 0$ is$

questions.solution:
Given,&

\left(5 + x\right)500 + x\left(5 + x\right)499 + x^{2}\left(5 + x\right)498 + \ldots \ldots + x^{500}$

Using sum of the G.P in the given expression we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(5 + x\right)500\left[\left(\dfrac{x}{5 + x}\right)501 - 1\right]}{\left(\dfrac{x}{5 + x}\right) - 1} = \dfrac{x^{501} - \left(5 + x\right)501}{- 5}$

$= \dfrac{1}{5}\left(5 + x\right)501 - \dfrac{x501}{5}$

Now coefficient of $x^{101}$~in $\dfrac{1}{5} \left(5 + x\right)501$~will be~\dfrac{1}{5} \left($C101 501\right)\left($5\right)501 - 101= {5}^{399} \left($C101 501\right)$

$

questions.q: The term independent of $x$ in the expansion of \left(\dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{x^{8}}{81}\right) . {\left(2x^{2} - \dfrac{3}{x^{2}}\right)}^{6}$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$To find the coefficient of term independent of $x$ in given expression, first let's find constant term and coefficient of $x^{- 8}$ in the expansion of ${\left(2x^{2} - \dfrac{3}{x^{2}}\right)}^{6}$
${T}_{r + 1}{=}^{6}{C}_{r}{\left(2x^{2}\right)}^{6 - r} \times {\left(- \dfrac{3}{x^{2}}\right)}^{r}$
${T}_{r + 1}{=}^{6}{C}_{r}{2}^{6 - r} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{r} \times x^{12 - 4r}$
For constant term: $r = 3$ , hence constant term = ${}^{6}{C}_{3}{2}^{3} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{3} \times x^{0}$
For coefficient of $x^{- 8}: r = 5$ , hence coefficient of $x^{- 8}{=}^{6}{C}_{5} \times {2}^{1}{\left(- 3\right)}^{5} \times x^{- 8}$
Given expression can be written as
\left(\dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{x^{8}}{81}\right)\left({}^{6}{C}_{3} \times {2}^{3} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{3} \times x^{0} + \ldots + {}^{6}{C}_{5} \times {2}^{1} \times { \left(-3\right)}^{5} \timesx^{- 8} + \ldots\right)$
Hence, coefficient of term independent of $x$
=\dfrac{1}{60}{\times}^{6}{C}_{3} \times {2}^{3}{\left(- 3\right)}^{3} - \dfrac{1}{81}{\times}^{6}{C}_{5} \times {2}^{1} \times {\left(- 3\right)}^{5}
$= - 72 + 36 = - 36$

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 10 \left(\dfrac{- k}{x2}\right)r\left(\sqrt{x}\right)10 - r$

$= Cr \cdot 10 \left(- k\right)r \cdot x^{5 - \dfrac{5r}{2}}$

for constant term

questions.solution:
General term of the binomial expansion of ${\left(2x^{3} - \dfrac{1}{3x^{2}}\right)}^{5}$ is

${T}_{r + 1} = {5}_{{C}_{r}} ( 2x^{3}{)}^{5 - r}{\left(\dfrac{- 1}{3x^{2}}\right)}^{r}$

For coefficient of $x^{5}$, we must have

$15 - 5r = 5 ⇒ r = 2$

So, required coefficient is

$= C2 5 ( 2{)}^{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{9}\right) = 10 \times 8 \times \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{80}{9}$

questions.q: For the natural numbers $m, n,$~if~$( 1 - y{)}^{m} ( 1 + y{)}^{n} = 1 + {a}_{1}y + {a}_{2}y^{2} + \ldots . + {a}_{m + n}y^{m + n}$~and ${a}_{1} = {a}_{2} = 10,$~then the value of $m + n,$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$( 1 - y{)}^{m} ( 1 + y{)}^{n}$

$= \left($C0 m - C1 m y + C2 m y^{2} + . . . + Cm m \left(- 1\right)my^{m}\right)\left(C0 n + C1 n y + C2 n y^{2} + . . . + Cn n y^{n}\right)$

Coefficient of $y \left({a}_{1}\right) =1 \cdotC1 n + C1 m ( - 1 )$

$= n - m = 10 \ldots \left(1\right)$

Coefficient of $y^{2} \left({a}_{2}\right)

$= 1 C2 n - C1 m C1 n + {1}^{m}{C}_{2} = 10$

$⇒ \dfrac{n ( n - 1 )}{2} -m \cdotn + \dfrac{m ( m - 1 )}{2} =10$

$⇒ m^{2} + n^{2} - 2mn - ( n + m ) = 20$

$⇒ ( n - m{)}^{2} - ( n + m ) = 20$

$⇒ n + m = 80 \ldots \left(2\right)$

By equation \left($1\right)$~and~ \left($2\right)$

$m = 35, n = 45$

Hence,~$m + n = 80

$

$\begin{aligned} & \left(x+\sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5+\left(x-\sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5 \\ & -\left[{ }^5 C_0 x^5+{ }^5 C_1 x^4\left(\sqrt{x^3-1}\right)+\ldots \ldots+{ }^5 C_5\left(\sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5\right]+ \\ & {\left[{ }^5 C_0 x^5-{ }^5 C_1 x^4\left(\sqrt{x^3-1}\right)+\ldots \ldots .+{ }^{-5} C_5\left(\sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5\right]} \\ & =2\left[x^5+{ }^5 C_2 x^3\left(x^3-1\right)+{ }^5 C_4\left(x^3-1\right)^2\right] \\ & =10 x^7+20 x^6+2 x^5-20 x^4-20 x^3+10 x \end{aligned}$ Now $\alpha=10, \beta=2, \gamma=-20, \delta=10$ Also, $\begin{aligned} & \left.
10 u+2 v=18
-20 u+10 v=20

questions.q: If the coefficients of $x^{7}$~in \left(ax^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2bx}\right)11$~and $x^{- 7}$~in \left(ax - \dfrac{1}{3bx^{2}}\right)11$& are equal, then
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The coefficient& of& $x^{7}$~in~\left(ax^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2bx}\right)11$~and~\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{3bx^{2}}\right)11$~are equal, then

${T}_{r + 1}{=}^{11}{C}_{r}\left(ax^{2}\right)11 - r\left(\dfrac{1}{2bx}\right)r$

${=}^{11}{C}_{r}\left(a\right)11 - r\left(\dfrac{1}{2b}\right)rx^{22 - 3r}$

Now solving~$22 - 3r = 7 ⇒ r = 5$

Coefficient of~$x^{- 7}$~in~\left(ax - \dfrac{1}{3bx^{2}}\right)11$

${T}_{r + 1}{=}^{11}{C}_{r}\left(ax\right)11 - r\left(- \dfrac{1}{3bx^{2}}\right)r$

${=}^{11}{C}_{r}a^{11 - r}\left(- \dfrac{1}{3b}\right)rx^{11 - 3r}$

Now solving~$11 - 3r = - 7 ⇒ r = 6$

Now equating coefficient of~$x^{7}$~and~$x^{- 7}$~we get,

$∴ { }^{11}{C}_{5}\left(a\right)6\left(\dfrac{1}{2b}\right)5{=}^{11}{C}_{6}a^{5}\left(- \dfrac{1}{3b}\right)6$

$⇒ {3}^{6}ab = 32$

$⇒ 729ab = 32$

Hence this is the correct option.

$

questions.q: Let $n \ge 5$~be an integer. If ${9}^{n} - 8n - 1 = 64\alpha$ and~${6}^{n} - 5n - 1 = 25\beta$, then~$\alpha - \beta$& is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Using the binomial expansion& \left(1 + x\right)n = C0 n + C1 n x + C2 n x^{2} . . . . . . . + Cn n x^{n}$

We get,

$\alpha = \dfrac{\left(1 + 8\right){}^{n} - 8n - 1}{64} = C2 n + C3 n 8 + C4 n {8}^{2} + \ldots$Similarly~$\beta = C2 n + C3 n 5 + C4 n {5}^{2} + \ldots .$

So~$\alpha - \beta =C3 n \left($8 - 5\right) + C4 n \left({8}^{2} - {5}^{2}\right) + \ldots + Cn n \left({8}^{n - 2} - {5}^{n - 2}\right)

So, option (C)& is the answer.

$

questions.q: The positive value of $\lambda$ for which the co-efficient of $x^{2}$ in the expansion $x^{2}\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{λ}{x2}\right)10$ is $720,$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $x^{2}{\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{\lambda}{x^{2}}\right)}^{10}$

= coefficient of $x^{0}$ in ${\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{\lambda}{x^{2}}\right)}^{10}$

A general term in the expansion ${\left(\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{\lambda}{x^{2}}\right)}^{10}$ is $10{C}_{r}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)10 - r\left(\dfrac{λ}{x2}\right)r{=}^{10}{C}_{r}\left(\lambda\right)r\left(x\right)5 - 5\dfrac{r}{2}$

$⇒$ coefficient of $x^{0} = {}^{10}{C}_{2}{\lambda}^{2}$ (for $r = 2$ )

$= 45{\lambda}^{2}$

Now $45{\lambda}^{2} = 720$

$⇒ \lambda = \pm 4$

questions.q: If the coefficients of $x^{7}$ in~\left(x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{bx}\right)11$~and $x^{- 7}$~in \left(x - \dfrac{1}{bx^{2}}\right)11, b \ne 0,$~are equal, then the value of $b$& is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Coefficient of& $x^{7}$~in~\left(x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{bx}\right)11$

$= Cr 11 \left(x^{2}\right)11 - r \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{bx}\right)r$

$= Cr 11 x^{22 - 3r} \cdot \dfrac{1}{br}$

So,~$22 - 3r = 7$

$⇒ r = 5$

So, the term is~$C5 11 \cdot \dfrac{1}{b5} \cdot x^{7}$

Coefficient of~$x^{- 7}$~in~\left(x - \dfrac{1}{bx^{2}}\right)11$

$= Cr 11 \left(x\right)11 - r \cdot \left(- \dfrac{1}{bx^{2}}\right)r$

$= Cr 11 x^{11 - 3r} \cdot \dfrac{\left(- 1\right)r}{br}$

So,~$11 - 3r = - 7 ∴ r = 6$

So, the term is~$C6 11 \cdot \dfrac{1}{b6}x^{- 7}$

Hence,~$C5 11 \cdot \dfrac{1}{b5} = C6 11 \cdot \dfrac{1}{b6}$

Since~$b \ne 0 ∴ b = 1$

questions.q: Let $m\text{and}n$ be the coefficients of seventh and thirteenth terms respectively in the expansion of \left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2x\dfrac{2}{3}}\right)18$. Then \left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$ is:

questions.solution:
Given expansion is \left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2x^{\dfrac{2}{3}}}\right)18$.

$⇒ {T}_{7} = C6 18 \left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\dfrac{1}{3}\right)12\left(\dfrac{1}{2x^{\dfrac{2}{3}}}\right)6$

$⇒ m = C6 18 \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)12\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)6$

$⇒ {T}_{13} = C12 18 \left(\dfrac{1}{3}x\dfrac{1}{3}\right)6\left(\dfrac{1}{2x^{\dfrac{2}{3}}}\right)12$

$⇒ n = C12 18 \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)6\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)12$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{C6 18 \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)12\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)6}{C12 18 \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)6\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)12}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)6}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)6}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m}{n} = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)6$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{m}{n}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{4}{9}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{n}{m}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{9}{4}$

$

questions.q: If the coefficients of $x$~and $x^{2}$ in $( 1 + x{)}^{p} ( 1 - x{)}^{q}$ are $4$~and $- 5$ respectively, then $2p + 3q$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given that& The coefficient of& $x$~and~$x^{2}$~in~\left(1 + x\right)p\left(1 - x\right)q$~are~$4$~and~$- 5$.

$⇒ \left($1 + x\right)p \left(1 - x\right)q = \left(1 + px + $\dfrac{p\left(p - 1\right)}{2 !}$x^{2} + . . . .\right) \left(1 - qx + \dfrac{q \left(q - 1\right)}${2 !}$x^{2} - . . . .\right)$

Now coefficient of~$x$~from the above expansion will be

$p - q$~which is equal to~$4$

$⇒ p - q = 4$.

Similarly coefficient of~$x^{2}$~is~$- 5$.

$⇒ \dfrac{p\left(p - 1\right)}{2} + \dfrac{q\left(q - 1\right)}{2} -pq = - 5$

$⇒ \dfrac{p^{2} - 2pq + q^{2}}{2} - \left(p + q\right)2 = - 5$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(p - q\right)2}{2} - \left(p + q\right)2 = - 5$

$⇒ \dfrac{16}{2} +5 = \left(p + q\right)2$

$⇒ p + q = 26$~and~$p - q = 4$

On solving the above equations we get,

$p = 15$~and~$q = 11$.

$⇒ 2p + 3q = 2\left(15\right) + 3\left(11\right) = 63$

Therefore, the required answer is~$63$.

$

questions.q: If in the expansion of $(1+x)^{\mathrm{p}}(1-x)^{\mathrm{q}}$, the coefficients of $x$ and $x^2$ are 1 and -2 , respectively, then $\mathrm{p}^2+\mathrm{q}^2$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & (1+\mathrm{x})^{\mathrm{p}}(1-\mathrm{x})^{\mathrm{q}}=\left({ }^{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{C}_0+{ }^{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{x}+{ }^{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{x}^2+\ldots\right)\left({ }^{\mathrm{q}} \mathrm{C}_0-{ }^{\mathrm{q}} \mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{x}+{ }^{\mathrm{q}} \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{x}^2+\ldots\right) \\ & \text { coff of } \mathrm{x} \equiv{ }^{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{C}_0{ }^{\mathrm{q}} \mathrm{C}_1+{ }^{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{C}_1{ }^{\mathrm{q}} \mathrm{C}_0=1 \\ & \mathrm{p}-\mathrm{q}=1 \\ & \text { coff of } \mathrm{x}^2 \equiv{ }^{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{C}_0{ }^{\mathrm{q}} \mathrm{C}_2-{ }^{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{C}_1{ }^{\mathrm{q}} \mathrm{C}_1+{ }^{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{C}_2{ }^{\mathrm{q}} \mathrm{C}_0=-2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{q}(\mathrm{q}-1)}{2}-\mathrm{pq}+\frac{\mathrm{p}(\mathrm{p}-1)}{2}=-2 \\ & \mathrm{q}^2-\mathrm{q}-2 \mathrm{pq}+\mathrm{p}^2-\mathrm{p}=-4 \\ & 1-(\mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q})=-4 \\ & \mathrm{p}+\mathrm{q}=5 \\ & \mathrm{p}=3 \\ & \mathrm{q}=2 \\ & \text { so } \mathrm{p}^2+\mathrm{q}^2=13\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let the coefficients of $x^{- 1}$ and $x^{- 3}$ in the expansion of~\left(2x\dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{x\dfrac{1}{5}}\right)15, x > 0$, be~$m$and~$n$~respectively. If~$r$~is a~positive integer such~$mn^{2} = Cr . 15 {2}^{r}$, then the~value of $r$ is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The& $r^{th}$~term of \left(2x\dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{x\dfrac{1}{5}}\right)15$

$⇒ {T}_{r + 1} = Cr 15 \left(2x\dfrac{1}{5}\right)15 - r\left(\dfrac{- 1}{x\dfrac{1}{5}}\right)r$

For term having $x^{- 1}$~

$\dfrac{15 - r}{5} - \dfrac{r}{5} = - 1 ⇒ r = 10$~$⇒ m = C10 15 \cdot {2}^{5} \cdot \left(- 1\right)10$

For term having $x^{- 3}$

$\dfrac{15 - 2r}{5} = - 3$~$⇒ r = 15$~$⇒ n = C15 15 \cdot {2}^{0} \cdot \left(- 1\right)15$

$∴ mn^{2} = C10 15 \cdot {2}^{5} = C5 15 \cdot {2}^{5}$

On comparing with~$m \cdot n^{2} = Cr 15 \cdot {2}^{r}$, we get~$r = 5$

$

questions.q: The remainder when ${19}^{200} + {23}^{200}$ is divided by $49$, is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Solving ${19}^{200} + {23}^{200} = {\left(21 - 2\right)}^{200} + {\left(21 + 2\right)}^{200}$

$= 2\left\{C0 200 {\left(21\right)}^{200} \times {2}^{0} + C2 200 {\left(21\right)}^{198} \times {2}^{2} . . . . C200 200 {\left(21\right)}^{0} \times {2}^{200}\right\}$

Now we know that ${21}^{2} = 441$ is divisible by $49$,

So rest of the terms will be divisible by $49$

So lets consider for $2\left\{C200 200 {\left(21\right)}^{0} \times {2}^{200}\right\} = {2}^{201}$

Now rewriting the term ${2}^{201} = {\left({2}^{3}\right)}^{67} = {\left(7 + 1\right)}^{67}$

Now ${\left(1 + 7\right)}^{67} = C0 67 \times 1 + C1 67 7 + C2 67 {7}^{2} . . . . . . . . .$

$= 1 + 67 \times 7 + 49k$

Now when dividing ${\left(1 + 7\right)}^{67}$ by $49$ we consider $1 + 67 \times 7$ as $49k$ is divisible by $49$

Now $1 + 67 \times 7 = 470$ which when divided by $49$ leaves remainder as $29$.

Now we know that ${21}^{2} = 441$ is divisible by $49$,

So rest of the terms will be divisible by $49$

So lets consider for $2\left\{C200 200 {\left(21\right)}^{0} \times {2}^{200}\right\} = {2}^{201}$

Now rewriting the term ${2}^{201} = {\left({2}^{3}\right)}^{67} = {\left(7 + 1\right)}^{67}$

Now ${\left(1 + 7\right)}^{67} = C0 67 \times 1 + C1 67 7 + C2 67 {7}^{2} . . . . . . . . .$

$= 1 + 67 \times 7 + 49k$

Now when dividing ${\left(1 + 7\right)}^{67}$ by $49$ we consider $1 + 67 \times 7$ as $49k$ is divisible by $49$

Now $1 + 67 \times 7 = 470$ which when divided by $49$ leaves remainder as $29$.

questions.q: Let \left(1+x+x^2\right)^{10}=a_0+a_1 x+a_2 x^2+\ldots .+a_{20} x^{20}$. If \left(a_1+a_3+a_5+\ldots .+a_{19}\right)-11 \mathrm{a}_2=121 \mathrm{k}$, then k is equal to $\qquad$ .

questions.solution:
\left(1+x+x^2\right)^{10}=a_0+a_1 x+a_2 x^2+\ldots .+a_{20} x^{20}\therefore 3^{10}=\mathrm{a}_0+\mathrm{a}_1+\mathrm{a}_2+\ldots .+\mathrm{a}_{20}$ ...(i)
$1=a_0-a_1+a_2 \ldots . .+a_{20}$ ...(ii)
$\text { (i) - (ii) } \Rightarrow a_1+a_3+\ldots .+a_{19}=\frac{3^{10}-1}{2}=29524$\begin{aligned}
\text { Also }\{ & 1+\mathrm{x}(1+\mathrm{x})\}^{10}=1 \\
& +{ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_1 \mathrm{x}(1+\mathrm{x})+{ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{x}^2(1+\mathrm{x})^2+\ldots .
\end{aligned}$\therefore \mathrm{a}_2={ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_1+{ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_2=55\therefore \frac{\left(\mathrm{a}_1+\mathrm{a}_3+\ldots+\mathrm{a}_{19}\right)-11 \mathrm{a}_2}{121}=239

questions.q: If the constant term in the expansion of \left(1+2 x-3 x^3\right)\left(\frac{3}{2} x^2-\frac{1}{3 x}\right)^9$ is $\mathrm{p}$, then $108 \mathrm{p}$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(1+2 x-3 x^3\right)\left(\frac{3}{2} x^2-\frac{1}{3 x}\right)^9 \\
& \text { General term } m\left(\frac{3}{2} x^2-\frac{1}{3 x}\right)^9 \\
& ={ }^9 C_r \cdot \frac{3^{9-2 r}}{2^{9-r}}(-1)^r \cdot x^{18-3 r}
\end{aligned}$
Put $r=6$ to get coeff. of $x^0={ }^9 C_6 \cdot \frac{1}{6^3} \cdot x^0=\frac{7}{18} x^0$
Put $\mathrm{r}=7$ to get coeff. of $\mathrmx^{-3}={ }^9 \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}} \cdot \frac{3^{-5}}{2^2}(-1)^7 \cdot \mathrmx^{-3}$\begin{aligned}
& =-{ }^9 C_7 \cdot \frac{1}{3^5 \cdot 2^2} \cdot x^{-3}=\frac{-1}{27} x^{-3} \\
& \left(1+2 x-3 x^3\right)\left(\frac{7}{18} x^0-\frac{1}{27} x^{-3}\right) \\
& \frac{7}{18}+\frac{3}{27}=\frac{7}{18}+\frac{1}{9}=\frac{7+2}{18}=\frac{9}{18}=\frac{1}{2} \\
& \therefore 108 \cdot \frac{1}{2}=54
\end{aligned}$$
